content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

Thanks for kicking this off. Before we get into any screens or features, I'd like to understand what you're really after, so we build the right thing.

A bookmark app can mean very different things depending on what's frustrating you today or what you're hoping to gain. So let me start with the "why":

**When this app is finished and working well, what would be different from how you handle bookmarks now?** For example — are you trying to stop losing links you meant to come back to, tidy up a mess of saved links that's grown unmanageable, find things faster later, share collections with other people, or something else entirely?

If it helps, you can just describe a recent moment where your current way of saving links let you down — that usually tells me the most.

I’ve accumulated lots of bookmarks across my browser, notes, and messages, and I often can’t find the right link when I need it. Recently I knew I’d saved an article for later, but couldn’t remember its title or where I’d put it.

I want one place where I can quickly save a link, have its basic details filled in automatically, organise it with tags and notes, and find it again by searching. I’d also like to mark things to read later, then archive or delete them when I’m done.

content:
That's really clear — thank you. The moment you described (knowing you'd saved something but not being able to get back to it) tells me a lot.

Here's what I'm hearing as the heart of it:

> **The real goal is being able to reliably find a link again when you need it** — today they're scattered across your browser, notes, and messages, so even things you deliberately saved get lost.

Everything else you mentioned — quick saving, auto-filled details, tags and notes, read-later, archive/delete — I'm reading as **the means** that make that findability possible: they exist so that when you come back later, the right link actually surfaces.

One scope check, because it changes what we'd focus on: **is the pain mostly about _re-finding_ what you've already saved, or equally about _getting things saved in the first place_** without friction so they don't end up scattered again? Both matter, but knowing which one hurts more tells me where the app should feel effortless first.

Does that framing of the goal match how you'd put it? Once we've got the goal settled, I'll ask one quick question about what kind of app you picture, and then we'll start walking through real screens together.
Yes, that framing matches. Re-finding saved links is the bigger pain, but saving should still be quick enough that I’ll consistently use the app instead of scattering links elsewhere.

content:
We've now settled **10 usage flows**, and the "what if" pass hasn't turned up anything that changes them. Here's the whole picture we've agreed on, in plain terms:

**Everyday use**
1. **Save a link fast** — paste an address, press Save, and its details are filled in for you; newest appears first.
2. **Find a link again** — search as you type across the title, address, site, description, tags, and notes, with matches highlighted.
3. **Organise with tags** — add tags as chips, with suggestions of tags you've used before so you stay consistent.
4. **Add a note** — one note per link, with bullet lists and links.
5. **Edit anything** — fix the title, description, tags, and note together in one panel.
6. **Read later** — mark links to read, see just those under a "To read" tab, and unmark when done.
7. **Archive or delete** — archive to keep something recoverable but out of the way, or delete permanently (with a confirmation).

**When things aren't perfect**
8. **Already saved it** — no duplicate is created; you're taken to the existing one (with a shortcut to edit it), or told it's in your Archive.
9. **Couldn't fetch details / bad input** — an invalid entry is refused gently; a valid link is always kept even if its details can't be fetched, and you can name it yourself.
10. **Empty and no-result states** — friendly prompts instead of blank screens.

I've also set aside, for later, some non-functional points you implied — that saving should feel quick, and that it should work well on both computer and phone.

**May I now start building this as the real application?** That's the point where I switch from exploring to implementing the scope above — I won't proceed until you say so.
Yes, that scope captures what we agreed and is enough to meet my main goal. Please go ahead and build the real application.
